scope: Independent source review of current NAV-SCAN reference provenance; no ROS publisher/Gazebo started.
findings: Current waypoint clears association before any new request; cumulative reference_requests is no longer acceptance authority.
Each reference Path header has a per-process strictly increasing immutable stamp, independent of mutable Bspline start_time.
SCAN reference_ready is cleared before processing; original requested body goal and stamp are committed only after successful global planning.
SingleThreadedExecutor prevents an interleaved local publish inside pathCallback planning/commit.
Both normal and emergency Bspline publishers emit matching full numeric payload metadata from the actual published message.
Global goal collision adjustment is recorded separately and never replaces the original mission arrival coordinate.
NAV accepts a pair only for its current reference and original body goal, with full order/id/start_time/control points/knots equality.
Bounded caches handle either topic arriving first; new reference clears both caches.
After pairing, controller still applies spline dimensions/finite/start distance/nondegenerate checks; actual LiDAR collision and raw SLAM arrival remain authoritative.
All request_plan paths invalidate samples before waiting for the new trajectory; no continued old samples on a new reference.
Measured-state replacement and zero planned stop boundary do not change measured start position or inject GT; GT remains independent mission evaluation.
additional_hardening_initial_findings: Same-reference pair replay 1 -> 2 -> 1 can regress accepted output without a monotonic accepted trajectory id. Normal ordered delivery from the current single DDS writer avoids this ordering; broader delayed/replayed fixture exposes it.
Non-object JSON metadata raises AttributeError before current callback error handler. A dictionary validation should reject safely.
limits: Provenance does not establish collision freedom or progress. Geometry and sensors must still pass their independent gates.
Run11 did not archive full historical Bspline payloads or the actual boundary acceleration; this is not an exact spline replay.
The run11 new replan111 east curve is supported by printed new-reference evidence and the independent polynomial fixture; metadata race is not claimed as its proven primary cause.
No complete three-floor exploration/return/F1-F3 mission PASS is established by this source/protocol review.
additional_hardening_resolution: Both findings fixed by navigation owner: accepted trajectory id high water rejects same-reference old pairs, and non-object metadata rejects safely. Independent protocol tests 12/12 with all 24 two-trajectory delivery permutations pass.
